def-qa-33-effective-finite-matrix-encodi:
## Definition

A finite-dimensional complex matrix input of dimension $d$ is **effectively encoded** if its complete binary description specifies $d$ and conforms to one fixed deterministic entry-approximation machine. Given the description, an entry index, and unary precision request $1^p$, that machine returns rational real and imaginary parts within $2^{-p}$ of the exact entry in time bounded by one fixed polynomial in the total description length plus $p$, uniformly over all valid encodings. Rational entries use their exact binary numerator and denominator; algebraic entries use a finite encoding compatible with this same evaluator and bound. A **uniform matrix family** supplies one polynomial-time description-generation procedure for each member. Hermiticity, dimensions, and norm bounds are promises on the exact matrices, not conclusions inferred from a finite approximation.

This interface includes finite output size and all approximation bit costs. It does not supply a matrix oracle, exact comparisons on arbitrary computable reals, or a free unitary implementation.
lem-qa-33-bernstein-square-root-bound:
## Statement

For each integer $d\ge1$, the degree-$d$ Bernstein polynomial
$$B_d(x)=\sum_{j=0}^d\sqrt{j/d}\binom djx^j(1-x)^{d-j}$$
satisfies $\sup_{x\in[0,1]}|B_d(x)-\sqrt{x}|\le(4d)^{-1/4}$. Consequently degree $d\ge1/(4\eta^4)$ suffices for uniform error at most $\eta>0$.
lem-qa-33-near-unitary-polar-correction:
## Statement

Let $U$ be unitary on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $M$ be an endomorphism with $\|M-U\|\le\varepsilon\le1/8$. Then $M$ is invertible and its polar unitary $Q=M(M^*M)^{-1/2}$ satisfies $\|Q-U\|\le2\varepsilon$. The inverse square root is defined by the positive spectral square root. When $M$ has effectively computable entries in fixed dimension, the inverse square root also has an effective matrix approximation: expand $(I+X)^{-1/2}$ at $X=M^*M-I$, whose norm is less than $1/2$, and truncate the absolutely convergent binomial series.
lem-qa-33-projection-lemma:
## Statement

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $S\subseteq H$ be a nonzero subspace. Let $H_1,H_2$ be Hermitian endomorphisms, with $H_2|_S=0$ and $\langle H_2v,v\rangle\ge J\|v\|^2$ for every $v\in S^\perp$, where $J>2\|H_1\|$. Write $\lambda_S=\lambda_{\min}(H_1|_S)$. Then

$$\lambda_S-\frac{\|H_1\|^2}{J-2\|H_1\|}\le\lambda_{\min}(H_1+H_2)\le\lambda_S.$$

Here $H_1|_S$ is the compression $P_SH_1P_S$ on $S$, where $P_S$ is orthogonal projection. Assume $S\ne\{0\}$ so that $\lambda_S$ is defined. If $S^\perp=\{0\}$, the lower spectral hypothesis is vacuous and the conclusion reduces to equality.
lem-qa-33-normalized-clifford-t-su2-pack:
## Statement

Use the exact one-qubit matrices $H$ and $T=\operatorname{diag}(1,e^{i\pi/4})$ of [[def-qc-one-qubit-gate-alphabet-and-rotations]]. The matrices $h=iH$ and $t=e^{-i\pi/8}T$, together with their inverses, are determinant-one representatives in $SU(2)$. Their generated subgroup is dense in $SU(2)$. Replacing each normalized letter in a word by its underlying physical $H,T,T^\dagger$ letter changes the product only by one scalar phase, so an unconditional one-qubit circuit can approximate every $SU(2)$ target up to an irrelevant global phase. A normalized letter must not be placed under a control without correcting its scalar phase.
def-qa-33-k-local-hamiltonian-promise:
## Definition

Fix an integer $k\ge1$. An encoded instance of input length $N$ gives $n,m\ge1$, with $n$ polynomially bounded in $N$ and $m$ polynomially bounded in $n$, and explicitly lists a finite matrix description for each Hermitian $H_j$ and its support on at most $k$ of the $n$ qubits. It also gives a positive rational polynomial bound $B$ with $\|H_j\|\le B$ for every exact term. Matrix descriptions and their approximation procedures use [[def-qa-33-effective-finite-matrix-encoding]]. Embed each local matrix by identity on unlisted qubits and put $H=\sum_{j=1}^m H_j$ on $(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes n}$. Given rational thresholds $a<b$ with $b-a\ge1/p(n)$ for a polynomial $p$, the promise problem has YES instances when $\lambda_{\min}(H)\le a$ and NO instances when $\lambda_{\min}(H)\ge b$. Inputs violating the format or promise are outside the promise; no behavior is required there. A matrix description is not a free measurement oracle: a verifier must generate every local test circuit from the finite encoding.
def-qa-33-witness-verifier-interface:
## Definition

For an input length $n$, let $X_n=\mathcal Q_n$ be the ordered classical-input register, $W_n=\mathcal Q_{w(n)}$ a witness register, and $A_n=\mathcal Q_{a(n)}$ a clean-ancilla register; $w(n),a(n)$ are polynomially bounded and zero qubits means the one-dimensional space $\mathbb C$. A verifier family is one full-list uniform family of finite circuits on $X_n\otimes W_n\otimes A_n$, generated in polynomial time from $1^n$. Its gate order and unitary denotation are those of [[def-qc-uniform-circuit-family]], [[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]], and [[def-qc-circuit-denotational-semantics]]. The first register holds the classical basis input $|x\rangle$, the witness may be any density operator $\rho$ on $W_n$, and the clean ancillas start in $|0^{a(n)}\rangle$. Thus this definition adds an explicit quantum witness register to the classical-input, zero-ancilla promise-computation convention of [[def-qc-promise-computation-model]]; a witness is not an initialized ancilla.

Let $O_n$ be the ordered tuple of distinct terminally measured wires. A total polynomial-time predicate $\operatorname{Acc}_n(x,z)$ determines acceptance from the measured output string $z$. Let $J_x:W_n\to X_n\otimes W_n\otimes A_n$ be $J_x\psi=|x\rangle\otimes\psi\otimes|0^{a(n)}\rangle$, and let $P_x$ be the orthogonal projection onto all computational-basis output strings accepted by $\operatorname{Acc}_n(x,\cdot)$, tensored with the identity on every unmeasured wire. Define the witness acceptance effect and its probability by

$$E_x:=J_x^*U_n^*P_xU_nJ_x,\qquad p_V(x,\rho):=\operatorname{Tr}(E_x\rho).$$

The projection $P_x$ sums over every unmeasured output wire. The positivity of this compression and its equality with the terminal outcome law are proved separately. The matrix input, gate list, generator, output predicate, and all circuit and classical costs are charged according to [[def-qc-circuit-cost-model]]; no intermediate measurement or free random source is assumed in this base interface.
lem-qa-33-finite-dimensional-unitary-syn:
## Statement

Fix a nonnegative integer $q$ and dimension $D=2^q$, independent of input length. Given a $D\times D$ unitary whose entries have polynomial-time Cauchy names from a finite description and a rational $0<\eta<1/2$, a deterministic polynomial-time procedure outputs a circuit on its $q$ data wires, with a constant number of clean ancillas returned to zero, for which there is a unit scalar $\lambda$ with $\|V-\lambda U\|\le\eta$. The procedure has polynomial bit cost and polynomial gate count in the description length and $1/\eta$. Scalar phase is immaterial only for this unconditional circuit. The construction uses complex Givens elimination with robust pivoting, a constant-width decomposition into unconditional one-qubit $SU(2)$ rotations and CNOT gates, and the finite-precision compiler of [[thm-qc-solovay-kitaev-bit-complexity]]. Its exact reversible-control subconstruction gives Toffoli from $H,T,T^\dagger,\mathrm{CNOT}$ by the parity-phase identity in the proof.
lem-qa-33-algebraic-term-rationalization:
## Statement

Fix $k$ and let $H=\sum_{j=1}^mH_j$ be an encoded $k$-local Hamiltonian with $m=\operatorname{poly}(n)$, local dimension at most $D=2^k$, and algebraic entries supplied by polynomial-time Cauchy procedures. For every rational $\tau>0$, a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm outputs rational Hermitian local matrices $\widetilde H_j$ with $\sum_j\|H_j-\widetilde H_j\|\le\tau$. Consequently $|\lambda_{\min}(H)-\lambda_{\min}(\widetilde H)|\le\tau$. If the original promise thresholds are $a<b$ with gap $\Delta=b-a$, choose $\tau\le\Delta/8$ and output thresholds $a+\tau,b-\tau$; the mapped YES and NO instances remain on their respective promise sides with gap at least $3\Delta/4$. A concrete polynomial running-time conclusion requires the stated polynomial-time Cauchy bounds for each algebraic entry encoding.
lem-qa-33-fixed-arity-local-measurement-:
## Statement

Fix $k$. Let $K$ be a Hermitian matrix on at most $k$ qubits with rational or effectively encoded algebraic entries of bit length $b$, let $B\ge\|K\|$ be a positive rational of bit length $b$, and set $E=(I-K/B)/2$. For any rational $0<\eta<1/2$, a deterministic polynomial-time generator in $b+\log B+1/\eta$ outputs a finite QC14 circuit with one flag bit whose measured outcome $1$ has effect $\widetilde E$ satisfying $\|\widetilde E-E\|\le\eta$. Let $U_0$ be the Naimark block unitary of the proof and define $U_{acc}=(X_{flag}\otimes I)U_0$. The construction supplies polynomial-time Cauchy names for $U_{acc}$ and a standalone dilation circuit whose unitary is within $\eta/2$, up to global phase, of $U_{acc}$. With one selector bit, [[lem-qa-33-finite-dimensional-unitary-synthesis]] compiles the full block diagonal matrix $I\oplus U_{acc}$ from those Cauchy names. Circuit size and generator bit time are polynomial in $b+\log B+1/\eta$. No local matrix is treated as a free gate or oracle.
lem-qa-33-uniform-programmed-circuit-int:
## Statement

Use the fixed QC14 alphabet $\{H,T,T^\dagger,\mathrm{CNOT}\}$. Let $M$ be one fixed deterministic polynomial-time classical machine that, on each binary input $x$ of length $n$, outputs a valid circuit description $P_x$ of at most $L(n)$ gate records on at most $W(n)$ data wires, where $L,W$ are fixed polynomials. Encode the output as exactly $L(n)$ fixed-width records: each record is either blank, a one-qubit label $H,T,T^\dagger$ with one wire address, or a CNOT label with an ordered pair of distinct wire addresses; unused address fields are zero. Let $\delta(n)$ be any inverse-polynomial rational tolerance produced by a fixed polynomial-time machine from $1^n$, with polynomial bit length. There is a full-list uniform QC14 family generated from $1^n$ which on classical basis input $x$ and data state $|\psi\rangle$ outputs a state within operator error $\delta(n)$, up to a global scalar, of
$$|x\rangle\otimes P_x|\psi\rangle\otimes|M(x)\rangle\otimes|0^w\rangle$$
for a polynomially bounded work width $w(n)$. Its size and generator time are polynomial in $n$ and $1/\delta(n)$. The program and arithmetic registers are terminal unmeasured wires; their presence changes the data-register outcome law from executing $P_x$ by at most $2\delta(n)$. This lemma converts a polynomial-time input-dependent compiler into the input-length-uniform verifier model.
lem-qa-33-witness-acceptance-effect:
## Statement

For every verifier interface of [[def-qa-33-witness-verifier-interface]], the compression $E_x=J_x^*U_n^*P_xU_nJ_x$ is a positive contraction on $W_n$. For every witness density operator $\rho$, its terminal acceptance probability, summed over every unmeasured wire, equals $\operatorname{Tr}(E_x\rho)\in[0,1]$.
def-qa-33-qma-promise-class:
## Definition

Let $\Pi=(Y,N)$ be a promise problem, $0\le s(n)<c(n)\le1$ efficiently encoded rational thresholds, and $w(n),a(n)$ polynomially bounded witness and clean-ancilla lengths. Require $c(n)-s(n)\ge1/p(n)$ for some polynomially bounded positive $p$. Then $\Pi\in\mathrm{QMA}(c,s)$ if there is a full-list uniform verifier interface as in [[def-qa-33-witness-verifier-interface]] such that every $x\in Y$ has a witness density operator $\rho$ with $\operatorname{Tr}(E_x\rho)\ge c(|x|)$, and every $x\in N$ and every witness density operator satisfy $\operatorname{Tr}(E_x\rho)\le s(|x|)$. Behavior outside $Y\cup N$ is unrestricted. The standard bounded-error class uses $c=2/3$ and $s=1/3$. The effect and probability are well-defined by [[lem-qa-33-witness-acceptance-effect]].
alg-qa-33-qma-parallel-majority-amplific:
## Definition

Given a verifier for thresholds $0\le s<c\le1$, an integer $r\ge1$, and an $r$-copy witness register, partition the witness into $r$ blocks of the original witness length and give each copy of the verifier its own fresh clean ancillas and output bit. Run the $r$ finite verifier circuits on disjoint blocks, measure their terminal accept bits, and let $S$ be their sum. Accept exactly when

$$S\ge\left\lceil\frac{r(c+s)}2\right\rceil.$$

The rational midpoint and integer threshold are computed exactly from the binary encodings of $c,s,r$. For an arbitrary initial joint witness, including one entangled across the $r$ blocks, the verifier evaluates the same finite product circuit; soundness for this case is established in the separate proof of the entangled-witness amplification result.
def-qa-33-feynman-kitaev-history-hamilto:
## Definition

Let a verifier circuit have $T\ge1$ gates $U_1,\ldots,U_T$, each acting on at most two computation qubits, with its accept/reject predicate reversibly computed into one output qubit (accept is $|1\rangle$). Let $N=T+1$ and encode time $t$ by the unary clock word $|c_t\rangle=|1^t0^{T-t}\rangle$ on $T$ clock qubits. For an initial computation vector $\phi$ define its normalized history
$$|\eta_\phi\rangle=N^{-1/2}\sum_{t=0}^T(U_t\cdots U_1\phi)\otimes|c_t\rangle,$$
where the $t=0$ product is $I$. For each propagation edge $t=1,\ldots,T$, let $|pre_t\rangle,|post_t\rangle$ be the local clock patterns which $c_{t-1},c_t$ have on their smallest common window: for $T=1$ these are $0,1$ on $C_1$; for $T\ge2,t=1$ they are $00,10$ on $C_1C_2$; for $t=T$ they are $10,11$ on $C_{T-1}C_T$; and for $1<t<T$ they are $100,110$ on $C_{t-1}C_tC_{t+1}$. Define
$$H_{prop,t}=\tfrac12\bigl(I\otimes|pre_t\rangle\langle pre_t|+I\otimes|post_t\rangle\langle post_t|-U_t\otimes|post_t\rangle\langle pre_t|-U_t^*\otimes|pre_t\rangle\langle post_t|\bigr),$$
where each clock ket is only on the displayed local window. For each local pre/post block, its quadratic form is one half the squared norm of the difference between the post component and $U_t$ applied to the pre component, so it is positive semidefinite. On legal clock words these patterns identify exactly the adjacent times $t-1,t$. Put $H_{prop}=\sum_tH_{prop,t}$. Define
$$H_{in}=\sum_{a\in A}|1\rangle\langle1|_a\otimes|0\rangle\langle0|_{C_1},\quad H_{out}=N|0\rangle\langle0|_{out}\otimes|1\rangle\langle1|_{C_T},\quad H_{clock}=\sum_{i=1}^{T-1}|01\rangle\langle01|_{C_iC_{i+1}}.$$
Here $A$ indexes initially clean verifier ancillas, and the output predicate is computed into the displayed accept qubit. The history Hamiltonian is the positive sum $H_{in}+H_{prop}+H_{out}+H_{clock}$. A propagation term uses at most two computation and three clock qubits; each other summand uses at most two qubits.
def-qa-33-qma-completeness:
## Definition

A promise problem is **QMA-hard** if every problem in QMA reduces to it by a deterministic polynomial-time many-one promise-preserving reduction. It is **QMA-complete** if it is QMA-hard and itself belongs to QMA. “Promise-preserving reduction” has the meaning of [[def-promise-preserving-reduction]]; no behavior is required off the source promise.
thm-qa-33-pure-witness-suffices:
## Statement

For a finite QMA verifier with witness acceptance effect $E_x$, if a witness density operator $\rho$ satisfies $\operatorname{Tr}(E_x\rho)\ge c$, then some pure-state density operator $|u\rangle\langle u|$ satisfies $\operatorname{Tr}(E_x|u\rangle\langle u|)\ge c$. Thus allowing mixed witnesses does not increase the completeness threshold.
lem-qa-33-feynman-propagation-path-gap:
## Statement

On the legal clock space spanned by $|c_0\rangle,\ldots,|c_T\rangle$, the propagation Hamiltonian of [[def-qa-33-feynman-kitaev-history-hamiltonian]] is unitarily conjugate to
$$L_T=\tfrac12\sum_{t=1}^T(|t\rangle-|t-1\rangle)(\langle t|-\langle t-1|)$$
tensor the identity on computation space. Its kernel is the uniform clock vector, equivalently the valid computation histories, and its first positive eigenvalue is
$$1-\cos\!\left(\frac{\pi}{T+1}\right)\ge\frac{2}{(T+1)^2}.$$
lem-qa-33-kkr-legal-clock-restriction:
## Statement

For $T$ clock qubits let $S_{legal}=\operatorname{span}\{|1^t0^{T-t}\rangle:0\le t\le T\}$ and
$$H_{clock}^{KKR}=\sum_{1\le i<j\le T}I\otimes|01\rangle\langle01|_{C_iC_j}.$$
Its kernel is $S_{legal}$ and every illegal computational-basis clock word has eigenvalue at least one. Let $H_0$ be the sum of the remaining weighted KKR terms, with $K\ge\|H_0\|$, and let $g>0$ be the soundness gap allocated before this restriction. Any integer
$$J_{clock}>2K+4K^2/g$$
makes the projection-lemma error strictly less than $g/4$. The clock penalty is 2-local even though it has $O(T^2)$ summands.
thm-qa-33-qma-amplification-entangled-wi:
## Statement

Let a QMA verifier have completeness $c$ and soundness $s$ with $0\le s<c\le1$, and put $\gamma=c-s$. For $0<\delta<1$, choose an integer

$$r\ge 2\gamma^{-2}\ln(1/\delta).$$

Then the parallel verifier of [[alg-qa-33-qma-parallel-majority-amplification]] has completeness at least $1-\delta$ and soundness at most $\delta$. On a NO input its soundness bound holds for every joint $r$-block witness state, including entangled states. The repetition uses $r$ witness blocks and $r$ verifier copies, so choosing the least integer $r$ satisfying the bound gives polynomial size when $\gamma^{-1}$ and $\ln(1/\delta)$ are polynomially bounded. The probability bounds hold for every larger $r$ as well.
lem-qa-33-feynman-input-output-penalties:
## Statement

Let $N=T+1$ and let $|\eta_\phi\rangle$ be the history of an arbitrary normalized initial computation state $\phi$ for [[def-qa-33-feynman-kitaev-history-hamiltonian]]. Let $N_{bad}$ be the number of initially clean ancilla bits equal to one, let $p_{bad}$ be the probability that the ancilla register is not all zero, and let $p_{rej}$ be the verifier rejection probability at time $T$. Then
$$\langle\eta_\phi|H_{in}|\eta_\phi\rangle=\mathbb E[N_{bad}]/N\ge p_{bad}/N,\qquad\langle\eta_\phi|H_{out}|\eta_\phi\rangle=p_{rej}.$$
Moreover, the squared norm removed by orthogonally projecting $|\eta_\phi\rangle$ onto $\ker(H_{in}+H_{out})$ is exactly $(p_{bad}+p_{rej})/N$: the input constraint removes the entire dirty-ancilla component at clock time zero, and the output constraint removes the reject component at clock time $T$. In particular, a clean-ancilla history with acceptance at least $1-\epsilon$ has zero input energy and output energy at most $\epsilon$.
lem-qa-33-kkr-one-qubit-propagation-rest:
## Statement

Fix $L\ge2$ and let $T_2$ be the number of controlled-$Z$ gates. Pad the verifier to $T=(T_2+1)L-1$ steps, with controlled-$Z$ gates exactly at times $t=lL$ for $1\le l\le T_2$ and exactly $L$ clock configurations in each block $[lL,(l+1)L-1]$. Every other $U_t$ is one-qubit. For each one-qubit gate time $t$, define the KKR local propagation term by
$$H_{prop,t}=\tfrac12(I\otimes|10\rangle\langle10|_{C_tC_{t+1}}+I\otimes|10\rangle\langle10|_{C_{t-1}C_t}-U_t\otimes|1\rangle\langle0|_{C_t}-U_t^*\otimes|0\rangle\langle1|_{C_t})$$
for $1<t<T$, with endpoint terms
$$H_{prop,1}=\tfrac12(I\otimes|10\rangle\langle10|_{C_1C_2}+I\otimes|0\rangle\langle0|_{C_1}-U_1\otimes|1\rangle\langle0|_{C_1}-U_1^*\otimes|0\rangle\langle1|_{C_1}),$$
$$H_{prop,T}=\tfrac12(I\otimes|1\rangle\langle1|_{C_T}+I\otimes|10\rangle\langle10|_{C_{T-1}C_T}-U_T\otimes|1\rangle\langle0|_{C_T}-U_T^*\otimes|0\rangle\langle1|_{C_T}).$$
Each summand is at most 2-local. Put $H_{prop1}=\sum_{t:\,U_t\text{ is one-qubit}}H_{prop,t}$. On the legal clock space it is a direct sum of half-weight path Laplacians, and its kernel $S_{prop1}$ is spanned by block histories
$$|\eta_{l,i}\rangle=L^{-1/2}\sum_{t=lL}^{(l+1)L-1}U_t\cdots U_1|i\rangle\otimes|c_t\rangle,$$
where $i$ ranges over a computational basis of the work register and $l$ over the blocks. The nonzero gap is at least $g_1=1-\cos(\pi/L)\ge2/L^2$. If the remaining weighted terms have norm at most $K_1$, choose $J_1g_1>2K_1+K_1^2/\epsilon_1$; the projection lemma then incurs additive error below $\epsilon_1$ when restricting to $S_{prop1}$.
thm-qa-33-local-hamiltonian-in-qma:
## Statement

For each fixed $k$, the encoded $k$-Local Hamiltonian promise problem of [[def-qa-33-k-local-hamiltonian-promise]] is in QMA. A verifier receives an $n$-qubit witness $\rho$, uses the $\ell=\lceil\log_2m\rceil$ address qubits to choose uniformly one of $d=2^\ell$ addresses, rejects addresses $j\ge m$, and for $j<m$ measures the locally synthesized effect $E_j=(I-H_j/B)/2$. Its exact acceptance probability is
$$p(\rho)=\frac{m}{2d}-\frac{\operatorname{Tr}(H\rho)}{2dB}.$$
The promised acceptance gap is $(b-a)/(2dB)\ge(b-a)/(4mB)$ (with $d=1$ when $m=1$). Synthesize each conditional test to effect error at most one eighth of this gap; then the implemented verifier retains an inverse-polynomial gap and is uniformly generated from the term encodings. The QMA amplifier of [[thm-qa-33-qma-amplification-entangled-witness-soundness]] gives standard bounded error.
lem-qa-33-geometric-soundness-bound:
## Statement

Let $N=T+1$. Amplify a QMA verifier so that its NO soundness is $s\le1/8$. In the legal-clock history space let $S=\ker(H_{in}+H_{out})$ and $T_0=\ker(H_{prop})$. Then for every unit history vector $v\in T_0$,
$$\|P_Sv\|^2\le1-\frac1{2N}.$$
Consequently the least eigenvalue of $H_{in}+H_{out}+H_{prop}$ on legal clocks is at least $1/(2N^3)$. The proof allows arbitrary initial ancilla states in $T_0$; the QMA soundness premise is applied only to the clean-ancilla component.
lem-qa-33-kkr-two-qubit-propagation-rest:
## Statement

Assume the padded verifier has $T_2\ge1$ designated controlled-$Z$ gates and fixes an integer $L\ge5$, with $T=(T_2+1)L-1$ and those gates at times $t=lL$; if the source circuit has none, the hard-instance compiler can add a cancelling pair, after which this restriction applies. On $S_{prop1}$, let each designated controlled-$Z$ gate at time $t=lL$ be preceded at times $t-2,t-1$ by $Z$ on its first and second work wires, respectively, and followed at times $t+1,t+2$ by $Z$ on those wires. Since $L\ge5$, all clock indices $t-3,\ldots,t+3$ lie in $1,\ldots,T$. Each wire receives two $Z$ gates; they commute with controlled-$Z$ and square to identity, so the insertions preserve the verifier unitary. Write $P_a=|a\rangle\langle a|$, $P_{10}=|10\rangle\langle10|$, and $X=|0\rangle\langle1|+|1\rangle\langle0|$. Define
$$H_{qubit,t}=\tfrac12(-2P_0^{f_t}-2P_0^{s_t}+P_1^{f_t}+P_1^{s_t})\otimes X_{C_t},$$
$$\begin{aligned}8H_{time,t}=I\otimes[&P_{10}^{t,t+1}+6P_{10}^{t+1,t+2}+P_{10}^{t+2,t+3}+2|11\rangle\langle00|_{t+1,t+2}+2|00\rangle\langle11|_{t+1,t+2}+X_{t+1}+X_{t+2}\\&+P_{10}^{t-3,t-2}+6P_{10}^{t-2,t-1}+P_{10}^{t-1,t}+2|11\rangle\langle00|_{t-2,t-1}+2|00\rangle\langle11|_{t-2,t-1}+X_{t-2}+X_{t-1}].\end{aligned}$$
Put $H_{prop2}=\sum_{l=1}^{T_2}(H_{qubit,lL}+H_{time,lL})$. Each displayed summand is at most 2-local. On the four work sectors $00,01,10,11$, the restriction of $H_{qubit,t}+H_{time,t}$ to the two adjacent legal clock coordinates $|c_{t-1}\rangle,|c_t\rangle$ is respectively $2D_-,\frac12D_-,\frac12D_-,D_+$, where
$$D_-=\tfrac12(|c_{t-1}\rangle-|c_t\rangle)(\langle c_{t-1}|-\langle c_t|),\quad D_+=\tfrac12(|c_{t-1}\rangle+|c_t\rangle)(\langle c_{t-1}|+\langle c_t|).$$
Compression to normalized block histories contributes the common factor $1/L$. The table is positive and dominates the smaller table with coefficients $1/2,1/2,1/2,1$. Summing those smaller operators over blocks and basis labels gives
$$H'=\frac1{2L}\sum_{l,i}(|\eta_{l-1,i}\rangle-|\eta_{l,i}\rangle)(\langle\eta_{l-1,i}|-\langle\eta_{l,i}|).$$
Its kernel is the full correct-propagation space $S_{prop}$ and its gap is at least $g_2=2/[L(T_2+1)^2]$. If the remaining terms have norm at most $K_2$, choosing $J_2g_2>2K_2+K_2^2/\epsilon_2$ makes the restriction error less than $\epsilon_2$.
lem-qa-33-unary-clock-locality:
## Statement

For the unary clock $|c_t\rangle=|1^t0^{T-t}\rangle$, the penalty $H_{clock}=\sum_{i=1}^{T-1}|01\rangle\langle01|_{C_iC_{i+1}}$ has kernel exactly the legal-clock subspace and every illegal clock basis word has penalty at least $1$. With the local windows specified in [[def-qa-33-feynman-kitaev-history-hamiltonian]], every propagation summand is supported on at most two computation qubits and three clock qubits; input, output and clock summands are at most two-local. For any chosen remaining soundness gap $g>0$, a polynomial integer weight $J_{clock}$ makes the illegal-clock penalty change the least eigenvalue by at most $g/4$, provided the sum $H_0$ of all other weighted terms has a polynomial norm bound $K$; it suffices to choose $J_{clock}>2K+4K^2/g$.
lem-qa-33-kkr-initial-state-restriction:
## Statement

On the correct-propagation history space $S_{prop}$ of [[lem-qa-33-kkr-two-qubit-propagation-restriction]], the compressed input term is
$$H_{in}|_{S_{prop}}=\frac1{T+1}\sum_{a\in A}|1\rangle\langle1|_a,$$
where $A$ is the initially clean ancilla set, and the compressed output term is the reject projector $|0\rangle\langle0|_{out}$. Thus the kernel of $H_{in}|S_{prop}$ consists of histories initialized with clean ancillas. If $A\ne\varnothing$, its least positive eigenvalue is at least $1/(T+1)$; if $A=\varnothing$, the input term is zero and the restriction is immediate. If $K_{in}$ bounds the norm of the remaining output term, choose
$$J_{in}/(T+1)>2K_{in}+K_{in}^2/\epsilon_{in}.$$
Then the final projection-lemma error is below $\epsilon_{in}$. For an amplified verifier with YES acceptance at least $3/4$ and NO acceptance at most $1/4$, the compressed output energy is at most $1/4$ on YES and at least $3/4$ on NO.
thm-qa-33-5-local-hamiltonian-qma-comple:
## Statement

For fixed $k=5$, the rationally encoded local-Hamiltonian promise problem with polynomial term count, polynomial local norm bound, and inverse-polynomial promise gap is QMA-complete under deterministic polynomial-time promise-preserving many-one reductions. The reduction is the unary-clock Feynman–Kitaev construction of [[def-qa-33-feynman-kitaev-history-hamiltonian]], with the overlap correction in [[lem-qa-33-geometric-soundness-bound]] and illegal-clock penalty in [[lem-qa-33-unary-clock-locality]]. It outputs at most 5-local terms, polynomially many terms of polynomial norm, and explicitly computable rational thresholds. Algebraic gate entries are rationalized by [[lem-qa-33-algebraic-term-rationalization]].
thm-qa-33-2-local-hamiltonian-qma-comple:
## Statement

For fixed $k=2$, the rationally encoded $k$-Local Hamiltonian promise problem with polynomially many terms of polynomial norm and inverse-polynomial promise gap is QMA-complete. Hardness uses KKR's direct circuit-to-Hamiltonian reduction: penalize illegal unary clocks, incorrect one-qubit propagation, incorrect controlled-phase propagation, and nonzero initialized ancillas in that order. Every displayed summand is at most 2-local. If the four projection errors are each below $1/64$, the amplified NO ground energy is at least $3/4-4/64=11/16$, while YES energy is at most $1/4$. The resulting gap is at least $7/16$ before rationalization; [[lem-qa-33-algebraic-term-rationalization]] yields a rational instance with inverse-polynomial encoding and preserved gap. Membership is [[thm-qa-33-local-hamiltonian-in-qma]].
